mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
regime_hint: preemptive rate hike anticipation in inflationary cycle
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt equity market participants to expect higher corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 0.5% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: wage growth acceleration in labor market
failure_condition: During periods of high labor cost growth, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during low-growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures exceeding 2% of the prior quarter's value indicates strengthening demand momentum, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% over the current month vs prior quarter
failure_condition: Across 50 such consumption spikes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 95 triggers a supply-side risk premium as market participants anticipate production constraints, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: early-stage supply shock or capacity contraction
failure_condition: During confirmed supply shocks, 20-day forward returns do not show consistent negative performance (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 4.25% indicate persistent monetary tightening, which compresses credit conditions and elevates risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During such cycles, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 5.0% signals labor market slack and reduced wage growth expectations, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% in the current month
failure_condition: During periods of low unemployment, 20-day forward returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in monthly RSAFS retail sales above 3% of the prior quarter's level suggests excess demand, which can fuel optimism about corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 3% over the current month vs prior quarter
failure_condition: During confirmed demand booms, 5-day forward returns do not outperform the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST industrial production unexpectedly falls by more than 2% in a month, it signals supply-side weakness that can trigger a supply shock premium, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >2% in the current month vs prior month
failure_condition: During such events, 20-day forward returns do not show significant negative performance (p > 0.10).
